title: Christ the Man of Sorrows
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Christ the Man of Sorrows means that Jesus truly entered human suffering, grief, rejection, pain, and weakness. He is not distant from the afflicted, but the suffering Savior who knows sorrow and brings redemption through His own suffering.
summary: Christ the Man of Sorrows means that Jesus truly entered human suffering, grief, rejection, pain, and weakness. He is not distant from the afflicted, but the suffering Savior who knows sorrow and brings redemption through His own suffering.
christFocus: Jesus Christ bore grief, rejection, shame, pain, and death in order to save sinners and comfort His people. His suffering was not meaningless; through His wounds, God brings salvation, mercy, and hope to the broken.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Jesus is not untouched by sorrow. Scripture presents Him as the Man of Sorrows, acquainted with grief. He entered a world marked by sin, death, sickness, rejection, betrayal, injustice, and pain. He did not save His people from a distance; He came near.

The suffering of Christ was real. He wept at the tomb of Lazarus, agonized in Gethsemane, was despised and rejected, and bore the shame and pain of the cross. His humanity means He knows weakness and suffering from within human experience.

Yet Christ’s suffering was also redemptive. He did not merely suffer alongside sinners; He suffered for sinners. He bore sin, carried grief, endured judgment, and gave Himself so that guilty and broken people could be brought to God.

Because Jesus suffered faithfully, His people have a merciful High Priest. The suffering believer does not come to a Savior who is cold, impatient, or unfamiliar with pain. Christ knows sorrow, gives mercy, helps in weakness, and leads His people through suffering toward glory.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Suffering can make people feel forgotten by God. Grief, disability, rejection, trauma, sickness, addiction, loneliness, and church hurt can whisper that Christ is far away. This doctrine answers with the suffering Savior: Jesus came near enough to weep, bleed, die, and redeem.

This truth does not make pain easy, but it makes pain no longer lonely. Christ understands the afflicted, and He is able to comfort, sustain, cleanse, restore, and carry His people. The Man of Sorrows is also the risen Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring your sorrow honestly to Christ. Do not assume your pain makes you unwanted or unseen. Draw near to the Savior who suffered for you and now helps you in weakness. When comforting others, do not offer shallow answers; point them gently to the suffering and risen Christ who knows grief and gives mercy.
